question: Why do covalently bonded compounds have low boiling point?

options.text: Have strong covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force
Have weak covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force
Have strong covalent bond within molecules and also strong intermolecular force
Have strong intermolecular force within molecules but weak covalent bond

solution:
The correct answer is __**Have strong covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Covalently bonded compounds have strong covalent bonds within the molecules, which keep the atoms together in a molecule.
 
• Despite strong intramolecular forces, these compounds exhibit weak intermolecular forces between different molecules.
 
• The weak intermolecular forces (like van der Waals forces) require less energy to break, leading to a lower boiling point.
 
• These compounds usually exist in the form of gases or liquids at room temperature due to their low boiling points.
 
• Examples of covalently bonded compounds with low boiling points include molecular hydrogen (H₂), nitrogen (N₂), and methane (CH₄).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intermolecular Forces**

 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion which act between neighboring particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• Types of intermolecular forces include dipole-dipole interactions, London dispersion forces, and hydrogen bonding.
 
 
 
• **Boiling Point**
 
 
• The boiling point of a substance is the temperature at which its vapor pressure equals the external pressure surrounding the liquid.
 
• Strong intermolecular forces result in a higher boiling point as more energy is required to separate the molecules.
 
 
 
• **Polar and Non-Polar Covalent Bonds**
 
 
• Polar covalent bonds occur when electrons are shared unequally between atoms, leading to a distribution of charge.
 
• Non-polar covalent bonds occur when electrons are shared equally, resulting in no overall charge distribution.
